summary: POST /jobs/:queue enqueues a job without the target step's jobOptions, so a hand-posted or board-posted job gets no attempts, backoff or retention from its step
evidence: services/pipeline/src/server.ts:135 calls queue.add(body.name ?? workflow.entry, body.data ?? {}) with no third argument; Workflow.jobOptionsFor(step) exists and is used by flowJobFor() but not here. A 'backfill' job posted per plan §7.2 therefore inherits only the queue's defaultJobOptions.

summary: persistRecipeDraft enqueued the enrich job before commit whenever a caller handed in its own open transaction — the batch-import path, which is the highest-volume writer
evidence: services/web/src/server/recipe-import.ts:1275 opens db.transaction().execute(trx => ...) and calls persistRecipeDraft(trx, ...) at :1300; insertLocalRecipe uses inTransaction(), which reuses that transaction instead of opening one. The enqueue placed straight after insertLocalRecipe therefore fires pre-commit, the enrich step reads no recipe row and completes {status:'gone'}, and recipe_enrichment stays 'stale' until a manual backfill — silently dropping eager enrichment for every imported recipe (plan D4).

summary: plan §8.1's 'may_contain when the matched food's allergen trait is maybe' branch has no data behind it and is unreachable as specified
evidence: Open Food Facts' allergens:en: property is a flat comma-separated token list with no yes/no/maybe tri-state (unlike vegan:en:/vegetarian:en:, which do carry maybe) — measured over the pinned taxonomy: 74 allergens:en: lines, 13 distinct values, all bare tokens. traits.json therefore encodes al as a flat AllergenSlug[], and types.ts's IngredientTraits.al mirrors it. The other two may_contain triggers (text pattern on an unresolved line, ambiguous carrier) are implemented in full; this third one has nothing to evaluate.

summary: @buttery/food is unusable from services/pipeline: its moved modules use bundler-style extensionless relative imports, which Node's native ESM resolver rejects
evidence: Booting the local stack, both pipeline processes die at import time: "Error [ERR_MODULE_NOT_FOUND]: Cannot find module '/home/user/buttery/packages/food/src/aisles' imported from /home/user/buttery/packages/food/src/categorize.ts" (.dev-logs/pipeline.log, .dev-logs/pipeline-worker.log). The pipeline runs TypeScript directly under Node 26 with no bundler, unlike services/web, which is where these modules came from. Neither 'pnpm -r typecheck' nor any vitest suite catches it — both resolve extensionless specifiers.

summary: the dev enrichment panel renders illegibly: recipe content paints over it and its translucent background lets the page show through
evidence: Viewport screenshot at http://127.0.0.1:3000/household/recipes/01M0X3SMJSVYXMPVHV7HAVEKEM with a real enrichment row: the panel's 'ENRICHMENT - DEV ONLY' heading, its Status/Classifier/Enriched-at list and the ALLERGEN section are overlapped by the DetailPane's 'Instructions' heading, its numbered step badges and the 'Notes' heading. Two causes: Card carries bg-muted/20 (20% alpha, so the page shows through), and the fixed wrapper sits at z-(--z-banner)=40, below the header's --z-sticky=50 and whatever stacking context the pane establishes.
